domain: children's social care regulation / recurrent regulatory-inspection outcome prediction
prediction_question: For a children's home registered in England, given everything published about it in Ofsted bulk vintages released on or before instant T (prior full/monitoring inspection history with dates and judgements, registration attributes, and its owning organisation's portfolio outcomes in the same vintage), will the home's next FULL inspection after T be rated below Good (Requires improvement to be good, or Inadequate)?
prediction_time: The documented GOV.UK release date of an Ofsted bulk vintage (Europe/London). Features may include only what a vintage released on or before that date contains: prior inspections, judgements and registry attributes. Per-event 'Inspection publication date' columns exist in the 2024+ products; pre-2024 availability is anchored to vintage release dates from the GOV.UK 'Updates to this page' log (e.g. the Dec-2019 quarterly file, released 13 Feb 2020, is the first bulk source of Sep-Dec 2019 inspection outcomes). The target inspection is dated strictly after T, so no part of the target window precedes the prediction instant.
target_definition: Binary label from the overall judgement of the home's next full inspection after T: 1 = 'Requires improvement to be good' or 'Inadequate' (old 2016-2017 wording 'Requires Improvement' mapped identically), 0 = 'Good' or 'Outstanding'. Source column: 'Overall Effectiveness' (quarterly MI files 2016-2023) / 'Overall experiences and progress of children and young people' (annual 2024+ files and SFR files); this column is the label source and is excluded from shipped features. Homes that deregister before their next full inspection are censored, not labelled 0. Population: provision type children's home (incl. short-break-only, multi-building; 'children' in provider type), Active or Suspended in the feature vintage, with at least one prior graded full inspection visible in vintages released <= T.

split_strategy: Temporal splits on inspection dates of the deduped full-inspection event set (train 2017-2019 / eval 2021-2023 / holdout 2024-2026, 2020 excluded - COVID suspension with zero full inspections published). Both classes present in every year. Events cluster by home (repeat inspections, up to 3 within a quarter) and by owning organisation (multi-home providers) - clustered counts (distinct homes) recorded per year in notes.md; org-level clustering must be reported alongside event counts in qualification.

measurements.history_available: Dated per-inspection history IS published - the fsa-fhrs-next-rating blocker does not apply. Three overlapping bulk products all carry inspection-level rows with inspection number + inspection date + judgement: quarterly MI (Dec 2014 - Jun 2024), annual transparency (2024-2025), SFR annual full-year (2020-2026 editions; 2026 verified). Cross-product dedupe by inspection number verified twice: Jun-2024 quarterly file's 708 full inspections all re-keyed inside the 2024 annual file (708/708); SFR-2026 shared 2,084 events with the 2025 annual file and added 2,356 new.
measurements.event_volume_measured_2026_10_30: 16,760 deduped children's-home FULL inspections across the readable (CSV/ODS/XLSX-free) products, 2016-2026; per-year table in notes.md and probe/per_year_counts.json (2016: 728 / 2017: 2,122 / 2018: 2,195 / 2019: 1,206 / 2020: 0 / 2021: 1,466 / 2022: 1,302 / 2023: 1,641 / 2024: 1,660 / 2025: 3,268 / 2026 Q1: 1,172).
measurements.split_window_counts_measured: train 2017-2019: 5,523 full inspections, 1,200 positives (21.7%); eval 2021-2023: 4,409, 1,210 positives (27.4%); holdout 2024-2026: 6,100, 1,196 positives (19.6%). Prevalence drift documented (COVID-era deterioration 2021-2023, recovery 2025-2026).
measurements.label_mix_measured: Deduped full-inspection overall judgements 2016-2026: Good 10,916 / Requires improvement (both wordings) 2,811 / Outstanding 1,947 / Inadequate 1,085 / blank 1. Publisher cross-check: SFR 2026 main findings give 11% Outstanding / 71% Good / 13% RI / 5% Inadequate for 4,430 full inspections of homes of all types, 1 Apr 2025 - 31 Mar 2026; my deduped count over the same window is 4,440 (within 10 events, 0.2%; residual to resolve in construction).
measurements.publication_timing_measured: Per-event publication dates exist from the 2024+ products: children's-home events lag p50 41 days (min 15, max 127; n=2,399, 2025 file) and p50 40 (min 17, max 133; n=1,892, 2024 file). Pre-2024 files carry inspection dates only; the as-of policy anchors first bulk availability to vintage release dates recorded in the GOV.UK update log.
measurements.coverage_gaps_measured: Q1 quarters 2019-2024 unpublished in the quarterly series (partially recoverable via most-recent-inspection sheets and SFR full-year in-year sheets); Oct 2024 - Mar 2025 sits in the 2025 SFR (not yet pulled; same family); 2020 = zero full inspections (COVID); Dec 2014 - Sep 2016 editions are .xls (worker-side xlrd; not needed for splits).
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: Full readable series on the coordinator class: 22-23 anonymous GETs, 7,784,646 bytes (~7.4 MB), 5.1-9.5 s wall clock (probe/pull_series.py, probe/aggregate_years.py). Construction adds the .xls era and prior SFR editions: still < 25 MB total, coordinator-trivial; the labelled panel build belongs on a worker per repo convention.
measurements.schema_measured: Columns (2025 annual in-year sheet, 37): URN, provision type, registration date/status, region, LA, sector, places, supported-accommodation/short-break/multi-building flags, owning organisation, event type, inspection date, inspection publication date, event number, overall judgement + 4 domain judgements. Quarterly-era files (2016-2023): provider URN/status/type, sector, organisation, LA, region, inspection number, inspection date, type group, overall + 2-3 domain judgements. Provider name/address redacted in recent files; URN is the stable join key.
measurements.novelty_context: QMUL EMAP working paper (2025) predicts Ofsted SCHOOL inspection outcomes (state secondary schools, DfE attainment features) - different population/product. 'Outsourcing and children's social care' (PubMed 36201866, 2022) assembled 13k+ children's-home inspections 2014-2021 for explanatory regression on ownership vs quality - not a prediction benchmark, no splits, not released ML-ready. No ML-ready children's-home inspection-outcome prediction task found in web or mechanical searches (novelty_check below).

novelty_check.theirs: The publisher ships raw inspection-level rows (that is expected and fine). Academic use of the same source is explanatory, not predictive: 'Outsourcing and children's social care' (PubMed 36201866, 2022) built a longitudinal 13k-inspection panel 2014-2021 for ownership-vs-quality regressions, unreleased as ML-ready; a QMUL EMAP 2025 working paper predicts Ofsted SCHOOL inspection outcomes for state secondary schools from DfE attainment data (different population, features, product).
novelty_check.ours: The prediction task itself: a vintage-anchored, next-full-inspection below-Good binary classification for English children's homes, built from three Ofsted bulk products (quarterly MI 2014-2024, annual transparency 2024+, SFR full-year in-year sheets), with documented as-of policy anchored to GOV.UK vintage release dates, temporal train/eval/holdout on 16,760 measured events, censoring for deregistration, and scored baselines incl. the persistence reference. No one ships this task in ML-ready form.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

contracts.redistribution: supported - OGL v3.0 on every dataset page probed (licence_class A), quoted in license_evidence
contracts.prediction_timing: supported - prediction instants are documented GOV.UK vintage release dates; features are vintage-visible; targets are inspections dated after the instant; per-event publication dates from 2024+ and vintage-log bounds pre-2024; dated worked example in notes.md (T = 13 Feb 2020)
contracts.obtainable_target: supported - overall judgement of the next full inspection, from inspection-level rows published continuously since 2014; label source column named and excludable; censoring policy for deregistration stated
contracts.split_capacity: supported - measured 16,760 deduped full inspections 2016-2026; three disjoint windows each carry >4,000 events and >1,100 positives; both classes every year
contracts.not_a_mirror: supported - no existing ML-ready children's-home inspection-outcome prediction task; publisher ships raw data only; nearest prior art is explanatory (ownership-vs-quality regressions) or a different population (schools); see novelty_check

verdict.uncertainty: Persistence-baseline headroom is unmeasured (needs consecutive-inspection linkage = construction): homes rated below Good are re-inspected sooner and may persist below Good, the exact failure mode that killed defra-la-household-recycling-rate (rule solves task) and nhs-ae-four-hour-decline (rule beats model). A last-rating -> next-rating transition table and persistence reference must be the FIRST construction measurement, before any model figure is quoted. Secondary: label-vocabulary mapping across 2016-2027 frameworks; the 10-event (0.2%) residual vs the SFR denominator; Q1-quarter gaps (design already avoids conditioning on them).
verdict.next_action: Advancement owns construction: assemble the vintage-anchored event panel on a worker (pull all listed assets + .xls era with xlrd + prior SFR editions, pin sha256 per asset - the sibling 'Regulatory activity' series had a documented post-release correction, so vintage immutability is not assumed), then FIRST measure the last-rating -> next-rating transition table and persistence reference AUC. Ship only if headroom over the persistence reference is demonstrable; otherwise record the headroom finding and park. Expected artifact: train/eval/holdout CSVs on the next-full-inspection contract, vintage-anchored as-of ledger, fixtures asserting the SFR cross-check (4,430) and the COVID-2020 zero-full-inspection property.

next_action: Advancement owns construction: worker-side assembly of the vintage-anchored inspection-event panel (all products + .xls era + prior SFR editions, sha256-pinned), then the persistence-reference headroom measurement FIRST (last-rating -> next-rating transitions) before any model figure; ship only if headroom over persistence is demonstrable.
